भॄ: भॄ भॄ, cl. 9. P. भृणाति, बभार, &c., to blame; to bear, nourish, maintain, support, hold [cf. rt. भृ]; to fry; to bend, be crooked.
भेक: भेक भेक, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. भी), a frog, (according to the Kathā-sarit-sāgara XX. 77, the inarticulate sounds uttered by frogs were the result of the curse of Agni, who was betrayed by them to the gods when he took refuge in the water); a cloud; a timid man (= भीरु; cf. भेल); (ई), f. a female frog; a small frog; a kind of creeper, Hydrocotyle Asiatica. —भेक-पर्णी, f. ‘frog-leaved,’ a plant (= मण्डूक-पर्णी). —भेक-भुज्, क्, m. ‘frog-eater,’ a serpent, snake. —भेक-शब्द, अस्, m. the croaking of frogs.
भेकुरि: भेकुरि भेकुरि, इस्, f., Ved., N. of particular asterisms (according to Colebrooke ‘nymphs of the moon,’ cf. Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā XVIII. 40, Śatapatha-Brāhmaṇa IX. 4, 1, 9, where भेकुरि is explained by भाकुरि).
भेड: भेड भेड, or भेडक, अस्, m. (said by some to be fr. rt. भिल् with change of ल् into ड्), a ram, sheep, (in this sense also written भेड्र; cf. एड); a raft, float [cf. भेल]; N. of a physician; of a lexicographer; of a Ṛṣi; (ई), f. a ewe; N. of one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda (associated with Eḍī and Sameḍī in Mahā-bh. Śalya-parva 2631). —भेड-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain.
भेडर: भेडर, अस्, m., N. of an Agra-hāra.
भेद: भेद भेद, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. भिद्), breaking, splitting, cleaving, dividing, separating, dissolving; bursting, tearing, rending, piercing, perforation; breaking in or through, breaking open; violation, dissolution; interruption, disturbance; breach, rup-ture, fracture [cf. पर्व-भ्°]; a hurt, injury, wound; a slit, chasm, fissure, cleft, chap; division, separation, partition, part, portion; gaping, parting asunder [cf. हनु-भ्°]; discrimination, discernment; distinction, difference, kind, sort, species, variety; change, alter-ation, modification [cf. मति-भ्°]; divulging, dis-closure (of a secret), betrayal, treachery, treason [cf. रहस्य-भ्°, मन्त्र-भ्°]; dissension, em-broilment, disunion, disagreement, schism, making mischief, creating divisions (among confederates); seducing or enticing an ally to one's own party by sowing dissensions &c. (one of the four Upāyas or means of success against an opponent, see उपाय); defeat; (in philosophy) dualism, duality; (in medi-cine) evacuation of the bowels; (in astronomy) a particular separation of the stars; (कुक्षि-भेद, अस्, m., Ved. epithet of one of the modes in which an eclipse terminates); (in the drama according to the Sāhitya-darpaṇa) = संहति-भेदन, प्रोत्साहन; N. of a people (Ved.); N. of a man (see Atharva-veda XII. 4, 49); (औ), m. du. pudendum muliebre. —भेद-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, or भेद-कारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, or भेद-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, making a breach, breaking through, bursting asunder; causing separation, pro-ducing dissension or disunion, separating, disuniting. —भेद-तस्, ind. according to difference; discrimi-nately, according to peculiarities or diversities; sepa-rately, singly, individually, (opposed to युग-पद्।) —भेद-दृष्टि, इस्, f. viewing or holding the Universe and the Deity to be different and distinct. —भेद-धिक्कार, अस्, m. ‘refutation of duality,’ N. of a treatise by Nṛ-siṃha Āśrama controverting the Nyāya philosophy from a Vedānta point of view. —भेदधिक्कार-सत्क्रिया, f., N. of a com-mentary by Nārāyaṇa Āśrama on the Bheda-dhik-kāra. —भेद-प्रकाश, अस्, m. ‘manifestation of duality,’ N. of a refutation by Śaṅkara Miśra of the non-dualistic Vedānta theory from a Nyāya point of view. —भेद-प्रत्यय, अस्, m. belief in dualism (in opposition to the doctrine that every thing is God). —भेद-बुद्धि, इस्, f. perception or idea of a difference or distinction. —भेद-वादिन्, ई, m. one who maintains the doctrine that God and the Uni-verse are distinct. —भेद-विधि, इस्, m. the faculty of discriminating or discerning (between two different objects). —भेद-विभीषिका, f., N. of a philoso-phical work. —भेद-सह, अस्, आ, अम्, capable of being divided or disunited, seducible, corruptible. —भेदाभेद, औ, m. du. disagreement and agree-ment, disunion and union. —भेदोन्मुख (°द-उन्°), अस्, ई, अम्, just about to burst into blossom.
भेदक: भेदक, अस्, इका, अम्, who or what breaks or breaks open or divides; breaking, breaking through, causing division or separation; piercing; a mischief-maker; a destroyer; one who breaks through or diverts (the course of a stream, cf. Manu III. 163); distin-guishing, discriminating, defining; a distinguisher; (अस्, अम्?), m. n. an adjective; (इका), f. the act of breaking asunder, destruction, annihilation.
भेदन: भेदन, अस्, आ or ई (?), अम्, breaking, bursting, tearing, splitting, piercing, perforating, dividing, se-parating; loosening (as the feces, in medicine), dis-solving, cathartic, purgative; (अस्), m. a hog; a species of sorrel [cf. अम्ल-भ्°]; (अम्), n. the act of breaking or breaking asunder, bursting, splitting, piercing, cutting up, ripping open, dissolving, loosen-ing, fracture, rupture; the act of dividing or sepa-rating, division, separation, discrimination, making a difference; disclosing, betraying [cf. रहस्य-भ्°]; dissension, disunion, discord, disagreement; Asa Fœtida; (in astronomy) passing through a constel-lation or asterism.
भेदनीय: भेदनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be broken, frangible; capable of being split or cut open; fit to be separated or distinguished.
भेदित: भेदित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Caus.), broken, divided, separated.
भेदिन्: भेदिन्, ई, इनी, इ, who or what breaks or divides or splits &c., breaking, splitting, dividing, opening, dissolving; interrupting, disturbing; piercing, per-forating; hurting, wounding; loosening (the bowels), cathartic; separating, distinguishing; separating from (with abl.); causing to flow (as juice); having a dis-tinction or division; (in philosophy) one who sepa-rates spirit and matter or holds the doctrine of dualism; causing dissension; (ई), m. a species of sorrel; the ratan; (इनी), f. (with Tāntrikas) N. of a particular Śakti. —भेदि-त्व, अम्, n. separation, division, parting asunder.
भेदिर: भेदिर, अम्, n. = भिदिर, a thunderbolt.
भेदुर: भेदुर, अम्, n. = भिदुर, a thunderbolt.
भेद्य: भेद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be broken or split, to be divided or pierced or cut; capable of being broken or divided &c., frangible, divisible, fragile; to be cut or opened (in medicine); to be disclosed or betrayed; to be separated or distinguished; to be defined; to be set at variance or disunited; to be seduced or led away; (अम्), n. a substantive. —भे-द्य-रोग, अस्, m. any disease treated by incision or cutting. —भेद्य-लिङ्ग, अस्, आ, अम्, distinguished by the gender.
भेन: भेन भेन, भेश। See under 4. भ, p. 694, col. 2.
भेंपुर: भेंपुर भेम्पुर, अम्, n., N. of a Grāma.
भेयपाल: भेयपाल भेयपाल (?), अस्, m., N. of a king.
भेर: भेर भेर, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. भी), = भेरी, a kettle-drum.
भेरि: भेरि, इस्, or भेरी, f. (the latter is the more usual form), a kettle-drum; [cf. आभेरी।] —भेरी-घ्नत्, अन्, m. ‘striking a kettle-drum,’ a kettle-drummer. —भेरी-भाङ्-कार। अस्, m., N. of a poet, (perhaps for भेरी-झाङ्-कार।) —भेरी-स्वन-महा-स्वना, f., N. of one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda.
भेरुण्ड: भेरुण्ड भेरुण्ड, अस्, आ, अम्, (connected with rt. 1. भी), terrible, formidable, fearful, awful, (also read भेरण्ड); (अस्), m. a bird, (perhaps a parti-cular species of bird, also read भेरण्ड, cf. भा-रण्ड); a species of beast of prey (wolf, jackal, or hyena); N. of a form of Śiva; (आ), f., N. of a goddess (= काली); N. of a Yakṣiṇī or female attend-ant on Durgā; (अम्), n. conception, impregnation, pregnancy, (in this sense perhaps fr. rt. भृ।)
भेरुण्डक: भेरुण्डक, अस्, m. a jackal [cf. फेरु].
भेल: भेल भेल, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. भी), timid, timorous, fearful; foolish, ignorant, unwise, simple-minded; tall; active, agile; unsteady (literally or figuratively), inconstant; (अस्), m. a boat, skiff, float, raft; N. of a Ṛṣi (supposed to be the author of some medical works, cf. भेड).
भेलक: भेलक, अस्, अम्, m. n. = भेल, a boat, raft.
भेलु: भेलु भेलु, a particular high number.
भेलूपुरा: भेलूपुरा भेलूपुरा, f., N. of a suburb of Benares.
भेष्: भेष् भेष् [cf. rts. 1. भी, भ्यस्], cl. 1. P. A. भेषति, भेषते, &c., to fear, dread, be afraid; (according to others) to move, go.
भेषज: भेषज भेषज, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 1. भिषज्), making well or healthy, sanative, curative, curing (Ved.); (अम्), n. a remedy or cure, remedy against (with gen.); any drug or medicament, medicine, physic [cf. आस्राव-भ्°]; any spell or charm against diseases (as particular verses of the Atharva-veda); a kind of fennel, Nigella Indica; (according to Nai-ghaṇṭuka 1. 12) water. —भेषज-कल्प, अस्, m., N. of a chapter of the Aṣṭāṅga-hṛdaya-saṃhitā by Vāg-bhaṭa. —भेषज-चन्द्र, अस्, m., N. of a man. —भेषज-ता, f., Ved. curativeness, healing power. —भेषज-भक्षण, अम्, n. ‘drug-eat-ing,’ the act of taking medicine. —भेषजागार (°ज-आग्°), अम्, n. ‘medicine-room, drug-room,’ a druggist's or apothecary's shop. —भेषजाङ्ग (°ज-अङ्°), अम्, n. anything taken after medicine, any vehicle or medium in which medicine is administered (as water gruel).
भेषज्य: भेषज्य, अस्, आ, अम्, curative, sanitary, sanative.
भैक्ष: भैक्ष भैक्ष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भिक्षा), living by alms, subsisting by charity; (अम्), n. asking alms, begging, mendicancy, (भैक्षं चर् or भै-क्षाय गम्, to go about begging, beg); anything obtained by begging, begged food, charity, alms. —भैक्ष-काल, अस्, m. ‘alms-time,’ the time for alms or for bringing home anything obtained as alms. —भैक्ष-चरण or भैक्ष-चर्य, अम्, n. or भैक्ष-चर्या, f. the going about begging, plying for alms, collecting alms, begging. —भै-क्ष-जीविका, f. living on alms, subsisting by begging, mendicancy. —भैक्ष-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, eating alms-food, living on alms; (क्), m. a mendicant. —भै-क्ष-वृत्ति, इस्, f. the living on alms, mendicancy; (इस्, इस्, इ), living by charity. —भैक्षान्न (°ष-अन्°), अम्, n. ‘alms-food,’ food obtained as alms, begged food. —भैक्षाशिन् (°ष-आश्°), ई, इनी, इ, eating alms-food or food obtained by begging; (ई), m. a mendicant. —भैक्षाश्य, अम्, n. (fr. the preceding), the living on alms, subsisting by charity. —भैक्षाहार (°ष-आह्°), अस्, आ, अम्, eating begged food or food given in charity; (अस्), m. one living on charity (Manu XI. 257), a mendicant.
भैक्षक: भैक्षक (at the end of an adj. comp.) = भैक्ष, alms.
भैक्षुक: भैक्षुक, अम्, n. (fr. भिक्षुक), a number of mendicants, assemblage or collection of beggars.
भैक्ष्य: भैक्ष्य, an incorrect form for भैक्ष above. —भैक्ष्य-काल, भैक्ष्य-चर्य, भैक्ष्य-वृत्ति, see भैक्ष-काल, &c.
भैदिक: भैदिक भैदिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भेद), frangible, liable to fracture (? Pāṇ. V. 1, 64).
भैम: भैम भैम, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भीम), relating to Bhīma; (आस्), m. pl. the descendants of Bhīma; (ई), f. ‘the daughter of Bhīma,’ a patronymic of Damayantī; a festival on the eleventh day of Māgha, when ceremonies with तिल or sesamum are performed in honour of Bhīma; [cf. Lith. baime†, ‘terror.’] —भैम-प्रवीर, अस्, m. the bravest of the Bhaimas, the chief of the Bhaimas.
भैमगव: भैमगव, अस्, m. (fr. भीम-गव), a patro-nymic.
भैमरथ: भैमरथ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भीम-रथ), relating to Bhīma-ratha.
भैमसेनि: भैमसेनि, इस्, m. (fr. भीम-सेन), a patro-nymic of Divo-dāsa, (also written भैमसीनि); of Ghaṭotkaca, (also written भैमिसेनि।)
भैमसेन्य: भैमसेन्य, अस्, m. (fr. भीम-सेन), a patro-nymic.
भैमायन: भैमायन, अस्, m. a patronymic (see Scholiast on Pāṇ. VI. 2, 34).
भैमि: भैमि, इस्, m. (fr. भीम), a patronymic of Ghaṭotkaca.
भैरव: भैरव भैरव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भीरु), for-midable, awful, horrible, terrific, terrible, horrid; miserable; relating to Bhairava; (अस्), m. a form of Śiva, (eight forms of Bhairavas are enumerated, viz. महा-भ्°, संहार-भ्°, असिताङ्ग-भ्°, रुरु-भ्°, काल-भ्°, क्रोध-भ्°, ताम्र-चूड-भ्° or क-पाल-भ्°, चन्द्र-चूड-भ्° or रुद्र-भ्°; other names of these forms are sometimes given, e. g. विद्या-राज, काम-र्°, नाग-र्°, सच्छन्द-र्°, लम्बित-र्°, देव-र्°, उग्र-र्°, विघ्न-र्°); a man representing Bhairava; a Śivagaṇādhipa; a son of Śiva by Tārā-vatī (who was wife of Candra-śekhara, king of Karavīra-pura); N. of a Nāga; of a Yakṣa; of the author of the Pheṭkāriṇī-tantra; of a teacher of the Haṭha-vidyā; of two kings; of a hunter; of a river; of a Rāga or musical mode calculated to excite emotions of terror; (ई), f. a particular form of Durgā; a girl of twelve years (representing that goddess at the Durgā festival); N. of a Rāgiṇī or of a particular scale in the Hindū musical system; (अम्), n. terror, horror, the property of exciting terror, terribleness; = भैरव-तन्त्र below. —भैरव-कारक, अस्, इका, अम्, causing terror, formidable. —भैरव-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra men-tioned in Kṛṣṇānanda's Tantra-sāra. —भैरव-तर्जक, अस्, m. ‘awful threatener,’ an epithet of Viṣṇu (properly of Śiva). —भैरव-त्व, अम्, n. the state of being Bhairava or a form of Śiva. —भैरव-दीक्षित-तिलक, अस्, m., N. of an author. —भैरव-नाथ-तन्त्र, अम्, n. ‘Tantra of the lord of terror,’ N. of a Tantra. —भैरव-यातना, f. a purificatory torment inflicted by Śiva as presiding deity of Benares on those who die there, to render their spirits fit for absorption into the essence of the Supreme (whereas those who are punished by Yama have to return to mundane exist-ence). —भैरवाग्रतस् (°व-अग्°), ind. in the presence of Bhairava. —भैरवाचार्य (°व-आच्°), अस्, m., N. of a preceptor. —भैरवानन्द (°व-आन्°), अस्, m., N. of a Yogin. —भैरवेन्द्र (°व-इन्°), अस्, m., N. of a king. —भैरवेश (°व-ईश), अस्, m. ‘lord of terror,’ an epithet of Viṣṇu (properly of Śiva).
भैरवीय: भैरवीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to Bhairava (as a Tantra).
भैरिक: भैरिक, अस्, m., N. of a son of Kṛṣṇa by Satya-bhāmā.
भैषज: भैषज भैषज, अस्, m. (fr. भेषज), a sort of quail, Perdix Chinensis; (आस्), m. pl. of the patronymic Bhaiṣajya below; (अम्), n. a drug, medicine, medicament.
भैषज्य: भैषज्य, अस्, m. the descendant of a physician; a patronymic from Bhiṣaj; (अम्), n. the adminis-tering of medicines and healing applications to the sick; curativeness, healing efficacy; a particular ceremony (performed as a remedy for sickness); any remedy, drug, medicine, medicament. —भैषज्य-गुरु-वैदूर्य-प्रभा, f., N. of a Buddhist work. —भैषज्य-रत्नावली, f., N. of a medical work. —भैषज्य-राज, अस्, m., N. of a Bodhi-sattva. —भैषज्य-समुद्गत, अस्, m., N. of a Bodhi-sattva.
भैष्णज: भैष्णज, आस्, m. pl. of the following.
भैष्णज्य: भैष्णज्य, अस्, m. a patronymic from Bhiṣṇaja.
भैष्मक: भैष्मक भैष्मक, अस्, m. (fr. भीष्मक), a patronymic; (ई), f. a patronymic of Rukmiṇī.
भो: भो भो। See भोस्, p. 723, col. 3.
भोग: भोग 1. भोग, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. भुज्), any winding or curve, a ring, coil; winding; the ex-panded hood of a snake; a snake; the body; a par-ticular array, an army in column. —भोग-त्व, अम्, n. the state of being curved or winding, curvature, curvedness. —१। भोग-वत्, आन्, अती, अत् (for 2. see col. 3), furnished with windings or curves, having rings, ringed [cf. महा-भ्°]; (आन्), m. a snake; a mountain; (अती), f. a female snake-demon; one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda; the city of the snake-demons in the subterranean regions [cf. भो-गावती]; the sacred river of the snake-demons, or a Tīrtha in that river sacred to the serpent-king Vāsuki; N. of Ujjayinī in the Dvāpara age.

भोग 2. भोग, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 3. भुज्), en-joyment, fruition; eating; use, application; usufruct, the use of a deposit (Manu VIII. 149); utility, advantage, profitable aim or object; enjoyment (of women), sexual enjoyment; possessing, possession; ruling, governing, protecting, rule, government; cherishing, nourishing; suffering, experiencing; en-during, feeling, perception (of joy or sorrow), pleasure; suffering, passion; any object of enjoyment, that which is eaten, food; food offered to an idol; festivity, feasting, a repast, feast, banquet; income, revenue; gain, profit, produce; money, wealth; hire, the hire of dancing girls or courtezans, wages of prostitution; (in astronomy) the passing (of an asterism); the part of the ecliptic occupied by each of the 27 lunar mansions or Nakṣatras, i. e. 13° 20° or 800°; (in arithmetic) the numerator of a fraction (?); N. of a preceptor. —भोग-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, producing or affording enjoyment, procuring food or pleasure. —भोग-गुच्छ, अम्, n. hire of prostitution, price paid to harlots. —भोग-गृह, अम्, n. ‘pleasure-chamber,’ the inner or private apartments, women's apartments, zenana, harem; [cf. भोग-स्थान।] —भोग-ग्राम, अस्, m., N. of a village. —भोग-जात, अस्, आ, अम्, produced by enjoyment or by suffering. —भोग-दत्ता, f., N. of a woman. —भोग-दा, f. ‘granting enjoyment,’ N. of the goddess of the Piṅgalas. —भोग-देव, अस्, m. ‘having pleasure for a god (?),’ N. of a man (Rāja-taraṅgiṇī VIII. 531). —भोग-देह, अस्, m. ‘the body of suffering,’ the subtle body which a dead person takes with him and with which, accord-ing to his works, he experiences either happiness or misery. —भोग-नाथ, अस्, m., N. of a man. —भोग-पति, इस्, m. ‘lord of possession,’ a person in actual possession (of anything), the governor or viceroy of a town or province. —भोग-पाल, a groom; [cf. भोगिक।] —भोग-पिशाचिका, f. hunger. —भोग-प्रस्थ, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people. —भोग-भट्ट, अस्, m., N. of a poet. —भोग-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, enjoying pleasures. —भोग-भूमि, इस्, f. ‘land of enjoyment,’ the place where people enjoy the reward of their works, Svarga or paradise, (opposed to कर्म-भूमि, ‘land of works.’) —भो-ग-भृतक, अस्, m. a servant who works only for maintenance. —भोग-मण्डप, अस्, m. the part of the temple of Jagan-nāth where the food to be pre-sented to the idol is cooked. —भोग-लाभ, अस्, m. acquisition of enjoyment or profit; the gain or profit made by the use of anything deposited or pledged; welfare. —२। भोग-वत्, आन्, अती, अत् (for 1. see col. 2), furnished with enjoyments, having enjoy-ment, delightful, pleasurable, enjoyable, affording or yielding enjoyment; happy, prosperous; (आन्), m. dancing, acting and singing; N. of Satya-bhāmā's residence (Hari-vaṃśa 8978); (अती), f., N. of a town; epithet of the night of the second lunar day. —भोग-वर्धन, N. of a country; (आस्), m. pl. its inhabitants. —भोग-वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a king; of a merchant. —भोग-वस्तु, उ, n. an object of enjoyment. —भोग-सद्मन्, अ, n. the abode of pleasure; the inner or women's apartments. —भो-ग-सेन, अस्, m., N. of a man. —भोग-स्थान, अम्, n. the body as the seat of sensual enjoyment; the women's apartments. —भोगाधि (°ग-आधि), इस्, m. a pledge or deposit which may be used until redeemed. —भोगान्त (°ग-अन्°), अस्, m. the end of enjoyment or of suffering. —भोगायतन (°ग-आय्°), अम्, n. a place of enjoyment or suffering. —भो-गार्ह (°ग-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, fit for enjoyment, to be enjoyed or possessed; (अम्), n. property, wealth, money; [cf. भोग्य।] —भोगार्ह्य (°ग-अर्°), अम्, n. corn, grain. —भोगावली (°ग-आव्°), f. an encomiastic poem, the panegyric of professional encomiasts or bards, eulogium. —भोगावास (°ग-आव्°), अस्, m. ‘abode of pleasure,’ the women's apart-ments; [cf. भोग-गृह।]
भोगिन्: 1. भोगिन्, ई, इनी, इ, furnished with windings or curves, having windings or rings, curved, ringed [cf. महा-भ्°]; (ई), m. a snake [cf. कृष्ण-भ्°]. —भोगि-कान्त, अस्, m. ‘dear to snakes,’ air, wind. —भोगि-गन्धिका, f. a species of ichneumon plant. —भोगि-भुज्, क्, m. ‘eating snakes,’ an ich-neumon. —भोगि-वल्लभ, अम्, n. ‘beloved by snakes,’ sandal. —भोगीन्द्र (°गि-इन्°), अस्, m. ‘king of snakes,’ an epithet of Ananta or Śeṣa.

2. भोगिन्, ई, इनी, इ, enjoying, eating; using, pos-sessing; suffering, experiencing, undergoing; an enjoyer, possessor, &c.; full of enjoyments, devoted to enjoyments, indulging in sensual pleasures; wealthy, opulent; (ई), m. a voluptuary, a king, prince; the head man of a village; a barber; a person who accumulates money for a particular ex-penditure; (इनी), f. the concubine of a king or a wife not regularly consecrated with him; epithet of a kind of heroine.
भोगिक: भोगिक, अस्, m. a horse-keeper, groom (= भो-ग-पाल)।
भोगीन: भोगीन, अस्, आ, अम्, at the end of a comp. [cf. मातृ-भोगीण].
भोज: भोज, अस्, आ, अम्, bestowing enjoyment or pleasure, bountiful, liberal, (as an epithet of Indra or as the title of a king; Ved., Sāy. = फलस्य दातृ or रक्षितृ or पालयितृ); enjoying, leading a life of enjoyment or sensuality; (अस्), m., N. of a country (= Patna and Bhāgalpur, cf. भोज-कट); N. of a celebrated sovereign of Malwa (supposed to have flourished about the end of the tenth century or beginning of the eleventh century, and to have been a great patron of learning, see भोज-देव, भोज-राज below); a king of the Bhojas (see below); N. of a king of Vidarbha (Raghu-v. VII. 1); N. of a son of Vasu-deva and Śānti-devā; of Kṛta-varman; of a son of Ujjendra and founder of Bhoja-purī; of a lexicographer; of an author of certain medical works; of a son of Kalaśa-deva; (आ), f. a princess of the Bhojas; N. of the wife of Vīra-vrata, (also read भोज्या); a cowherd; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; the descendants of Mahā-bhoja [cf. महा-भ्°]. —भोज-कट, अम्, n., N. of a town founded by Rukmin (Mahā-bh. Sabhā-p. 1166); the country of Bhoja, the present Bhojpur, or the vicinity of Patna and Bhāgalpur. —भोजकटीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to or coming from Bhoja-kaṭa; (आस्), m. pl. the inhabitants of Bhoja-kaṭa. —भोज-कन्या, f. a girl of the race of the Bhojas. —भोज-कुल-प्र-दीप, अस्, m. ‘the lamp of the race of Bhoja,’ epithet of a king of Vidarbha (Raghu-v. VII. 26). —भोज-दुहितृ, ता, f. a daughter of Bhoja, a princess or queen of the Bhojas [cf. भोज-पुत्री]. —भोज-देव, अस्, m. king Bhoja (said to have been king of Dhārā in Malwa at the beginning of the eleventh century of our era; his capital being placed by some at Ujjayinī or Oujein; he was a great patron of literature, and is the reputed author of several works, e. g. the Yukti-kalpa-taru, Vyavahāra-samuccaya, Sarasvatī-kaṇṭhābharaṇa, and a commentary called Rāja-mārtaṇḍa on the Yoga-sūtras; cf. भोज-राज). —भोजदेव-शब्दानुशासन (°द-अन्°), अम्, n., N. of a grammatical work (mentioned by Ujjvala-datta, Uṇādi-s. 1. 92). —भोज-नगर, अम्, n., N. of a town [cf. भोज-पुर]. —भोज-नरेन्द्र (°र-इन्°), अस्, m. or भोज-नृपति, इस्, m. king Bhoja, = भोज-देव. —भोज-पति, इस्, m. the king of the Bhojas; king Bhoja (see भोज-देव); an epithet of Kaṃsa. —भोज-पुत्री, f. a daughter of Bhoja, a princess or queen of the Bhojas [cf. भोज-दुहितृ]. —भोज-पुर, अम्, n. or भोज-पुरी, f., N. of a town [cf. भोज-नगर]. —भोज-प्र-बन्ध or भोज-राज-प्रबन्ध, अस्, m., N. of Ballāla's biography of Bhoja king of Dhārā. —भो-ज-राज, अस्, m. the king of the Bhojas; king Bhoja (said to be the author of several works, and described as a poet, astronomer, lexicographer, and philosopher, cf. भोज-देव). —भोज-राजक-विवर्ग, अस्, m., N. of a work mentioned in the Śārṅga-dhara-pad-dhati. —भोजराज-वार्त्तिक, अम्, n., N. of a work mentioned in the Sāṅkhya-tattva-karumudī by Vācas-pati-miśra. —भोजराज-वृत्ति, इस्, f., N. of a com-mentary on the Yoga-sūtra by Patañjali (supposed to have been written under the patronage of king Bhoja). —भोजराजीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to or coming from Bhoja-rāja. —भोजाधिप (°ज-अध्°), अस्, m. ‘king of the Bhojas,’ an epithet of Kaṃsa; of Karṇa, the half brother of the Pāṇḍus. —भो-जाधिराज (°ज-अध्°), अस्, m. the king of the Bhojas. —भोजान्ता (°ज-अन्°), f., N. of a river. —भोजेन्-द्र (°ज-इन्°), अस्, m. the king of the Bhojas.
भोजक: भोजक, अस्, आ, अम्, eating; (fr. the Caus.), giving to eat, causing to eat, nourishing; (अस्), m. one who gives to eat, (perhaps) a waiter at table; N. of a class of priests (or Sun-worshippers, supposed to be descended from the Magas by intermarriage with women of the Bhoja race).
भोजन: भोजन, अस्, ई, अम्, causing or giving to eat, feeding, nourishing; (अस्), m. an epithet of Śiva; N. of a river; (अम्), n. the act of giving to eat, feed-ing, nourishing, serving up or dressing food, (in these senses fr. the Caus.); the act of enjoying, using, eating, (in these and other senses fr. the simple rt., cf. पर्ण-भ्°); a meal, food, (कु-भोजन, bad food, indifferent, viands); anything given as sustenance or for enjoyment, anything enjoyed or used, property, possession; any object of enjoyment. —भोजन-काल, अस्, m. meal-time, dinner-time, supper-time. —भोजन-त्याग, अस्, m. ‘food-abandonment,’ abstinence from food, fasting. —भोजन-भाण्ड, अम्, n. a dish of meat. —भोजन-भूमि, इस्, f. ‘eating-place,’ a place for eating. —भोजन-विशे-ष, अस्, m. choice food, a dainty, delicacy. —भो-जन-वृत्ति, इस्, f. course or act of eating, a meal, food. —भोजन-वेला, f. meal-time, dinner-time, supper-time. —भोजन-व्यग्र, अस्, आ, अम्, occu-pied or engaged in eating; bewildered or strait-ened for want of food. —भोजन-व्यय, अस्, m. expense for food. —भोजनाधिकार (°न-अध्°), अस्, m. superintendence over food or provisions, the office of a master or overseer of the kitchen, commis-sariat, stewardship, charge of provender.
भोजनीय: भोजनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be eaten or enjoyed, eatable, edible; (fr. the Caus.), to be fed, to be made to eat or enjoy; (अम्), n. food.
भोजयितव्य: भोजयितव्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Caus.), to be made to eat, to be fed or nourished.
भोजयितृ: भोजयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ (fr. the Caus), causing to enjoy or eat, feeding; one who makes another enjoy or eat; a promoter of enjoyment or amusement.
भोजयित्वा: भोजयित्वा, ind. having caused to eat, having fed.
भोजस्: भोजस्, Ved., in पुरु-भ्°, विश्व-भ्°; [cf. भो-जसे under rt. 3. भुज्, p. 713, col. 2.]
भोजिक: भोजिक, अस्, m., N. of a Brāhman.
भोजिन्: भोजिन्, ई, इनी, इ, enjoying, eating; using, pos-sessing, &c. (at the end of comps., cf. अ-श्राद्ध-भ्°, गृह-भ्°, भुजङ्ग-भ्°).
भोज्य: भोज्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be enjoyed or eaten, eatable, palatable [cf. प्रीति-भ्°]; to be enjoyed carnally; to be used; to be suffered or experienced; (fr. the Caus.), to be made to eat, to be fed or nourished; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (आ), f. a princess of the Bhojas [cf. भोजा]; (अम्), n. anything to be enjoyed or eaten, food, (कु-भोज्य, bad food, indifferent viands); a dainty; a feast, a store of provisions, eatables; enjoyment, advantage, profit. —भोज्य-काल, अस्, m. eating-time, dinner-time, meal-time. —भोज्य-ता, f. or भोज्य-त्व, अम्, n. the condition of being eaten, the state of being food; भोज्यतां या, to become food. —भोज्य-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of food. —भोज्य-सम्भव, अस्, m. ‘having its origin in food,’ chyle, chyme, the primary juice of the body [cf. रस]. —भोज्योष्ण (°य-उष्°), अस्, आ, अम्, too hot to be eaten.
भोट: भोट भोट or भोत, अस्, m., N. of a country, Bhoṭa (said to be the same as Tibet; cf. महा-भ्°). —भोट-देश, अस्, m. the country of Bhoṭa. —भो-टाङ्ग (°ट-अङ्°), अस्, m., N. of a country, Bhootan. —भोटान्त (°ट-अन्°), अस्, m., N. of a country [cf. भोटाङ्ग].
भोटीय: भोटीय, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to Tibet, Tibetan. —भोटीय-कोशी, f., N. of a river.
भोलानाथ: भोलानाथ भोलानाथ (?), अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva; N. of a commentator on the Mugdha-bodha.
भोलि: भोलि भोलि, इस्, m. a camel.
भोस्: भोस् भोस् (contracted fr. भवस् for भ-वन्, Sir! voc. sing. of 2. भवत्, q. v.; cf. भगोस् under भग-वत्, p. 696, col. 1), an interjection or vocative particle commonly used in addressing another person and generally translateable by ‘O!’ ‘Ho!’ ‘there!’ ‘Hallo!’ ‘Ah!’ ‘Alas!’ (before vowels and soft consonants भोस्, like भगोस् and अघोस्, is said to drop the final स्, but before vowels भोय् is also allowed, see Pāṇ. VIII. 3, 17, 18, 20, 22, Vopa-deva II. 49, 50; before hard consonants, भोस् or भोः is the form required, and भोः before a pause, but in the later literature भो is sometimes used where भोस् or भोः would be more correct; in Kathā-sarit-sāgara XVIII. 211, भोर् इति is against the rule; in Hari-vaṃśa 8301 भोस् occurs in the middle of a sentence, and in Bhāgavata-Purāṇa III. 23, 2, redundantly at the end; it is sometimes repeated, e. g. भो भो राजन् in Śakuntalā, p. 12; according to lexicographers it may be used as an interjection of sorrow and of interrogation.)
भोहर: भोहर भोहर, अस्, m., N. of a poet men-tioned in the Śārṅga-dhara-paddhati.
भौगक: भौगक भौगक, अस्, m. a patronymic from Bhogaka.
भौजकट: भौजकट भौजकट, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to or coming from Bhoja-kaṭa.
भौजङ्ग: भौजङ्ग भौजङ्ग, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भुजङ्-ग), relating to a snake, snake-like, snaky, serpent-like, serpentine; (अम्), n., scil. भ, the serpent asterism, the Nakṣatra Āśleṣā.
भौजि: भौजि भौजि, इस्, m. a patronymic from Bhoja.
भौजीय: भौजीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to or coming from Bhauji.
भौज्य: भौज्य, अम्, n., Ved. the rank of a king with the title of Bhoja.
भौत: भौत भौत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भूत), relating to existing beings; relating to or possessed by evil spirits, demoniacal, crazy, mad, silly; formed of the elements, elemental, material; (अस्), m. an attendant upon idols, a worshipper of demons and spirits, = देवल or देवलक, q. v.; (ई), f. ‘time of ghosts or spirits,’ night; (अम्), n. = भूतानां समूह, a collection or assemblage of Bhūtas.
भौतक: भौतक, अस्, ई, अम्, = भौत, possessed by evil spirits.
भौतिक: भौतिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भूत), coming from or relating to existing beings, belonging to created beings, (भौतिक सर्ग, the creation of beings, the corporeal creation); relating or pertaining to evil spirits; possessed by evil spirits; formed of the elements, produced by the coarse or visible elements, relating to the elements, elemental, existent, material; (अस्), m. Śiva (fr. भूति, ashes ?); a sort of monk; (अम्), n. anything elemental or material; a pearl (probably for मौक्तिक). —भौतिक-मठ, अस्, m. a college of monks, monastery, convent. —भौ-तिक-विद्या, f. ‘spirit-science,’ sorcery, witchcraft.
भौत्य: भौत्य, अस्, m. (fr. भूति), N. of a Manu; (अस्, ती, अम्), relating to the preceding Manu.
भौपाल: भौपाल भौपाल, अस्, m. (fr. भू-पाल), the son of a king, a prince.
भौम: भौम भौम, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भूमि), be-longing or relating to the earth, dedicated to the earth; existing on or in the earth, produced or com-ing from the earth or ground, earthly, terrestrial, terrene; consisting or made of earth, earthy; com-ing from the land (as revenue &c.); relating to the planet Mars or to his day, falling on Tuesday, (in this sense fr. भौम, the planet Mars); (अस्), m. water; light; ambergris (= अम्बर); a red flower-ing Punar-navā; a metronymic of several persons; N. of a kind of supernatural being or spirit haunting the earth; of Atṛ; of the Daitya Naraka; of the planet Mars, (वारो भौमस्य, Tuesday); an epi-thet of the twenty-seventh Muhūrta; (ई), f. ‘produced from the earth,’ an epithet of Sītā; (अम्), n. any-thing coming from the earth, dust, &c.; a particular mode of sitting practised by Yogins; = भूमि, ground, floor, ceiling, (at the end of an adj. comp.) —भौ-म-चार, अस्, m. ‘the course of the planet Mars,’ N. of the sixth chapter of Bhaṭṭotpala's commentary on Varāha-mihira's Bṛhat-saṃhitā. —भौम-दर्-शन-चार, अस्, m., N. of a chapter of the Mīna-rāja-jātaka ascribed to Yavaneśvara. —भौम-देव-लिपि, इस्, f., N. of a kind of writing. —भौ-म-रत्न, अम्, n. coral. —भौम-वार, अस्, m. ‘Mars-day,’ Tuesday.
भौमक: भौमक, अस्, m. any animal living in the earth.
भौमन: भौमन, अस्, m. an epithet of Viśva-karman, (for भौवन, q. v.)
भौमिक: भौमिक, अस्, ई, अम्, being or existing on the earth, earthly, earthy, terrestrial, terrene, belonging to any particular piece of ground.
भौर: भौर भौर, अस्, m. a patronymic from Bhūri.
भौरिक: भौरिक, अस्, m. the superintendent of gold in a royal treasury, a treasurer, (fr. भूरि, gold.)
भौरिकायणि: भौरिकायणि भौरिकायणि, इस्, m. a patro-nymic from Bhuriki below.
भौरिकि: भौरिकि, इस्, m. a patronymic. —भौरिकि-वि-ध, अस्, आ, अम्, see Pāṇ. IV. 2, 54.
भौलिकायनि: भौलिकायनि भौलिकायनि, इस्, m. a patro-nymic from Bhauliki below.
भौलिङ्गि: भौलिङ्गि भौलिङ्गि, इस्, m. (fr. भू-लिङ्ग), a king of Bhū-liṅga.
भौवन: भौवन भौवन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भुवन), belonging to the world; (अस्), m. an epithet of Viśva-karman [cf. भौमन]; a son of Manthu.
भौवनायन: भौवनायन, अस्, m. (fr. भुवन or भौ-वन), Ved. a patronymic.
भौवादिक: भौवादिक भौवादिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. rt. 1. भू + आदि), belonging to that class of roots which begins with भू, i. e. belonging to the first class.
भौवायन: भौवायन भौवायन, अस्, m. (fr. भुव), Ved. a patronymic; N. of Kapi-vana.
भ्यस्: भ्यस् भ्यस्, cl. 1. A. भ्यसते, बभ्यसे, भ्यसितुम्, Ved. to fear, be afraid, trem-ble [cf. rt. 1. भी]: Caus. भ्यासयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अबिभ्यसत्, to cause to fear, frighten: Desid. बिभ्यसिषते: Intens. बाभ्यस्यते, बाभ्यस्ति।
भ्रंश्: भ्रंश् भ्रंश् or भ्रश् (sometimes written भ्रंस्; cf. rt. भृश्), cl. 4. P. भ्रश्-यति (ep. also भ्रश्यते, &c.), cl. 1. A. भ्रंशते, बभ्रंश, बभ्रंशे, भ्रंशिष्यति, -ते, अभ्र-शत्, अभ्रंशिष्ट, भ्रंशितुम्, Indec. part. भ्रं-शितुआ or भ्रष्ट्वा, to fall, tumble, drop or fall down, fall out; to decline, decrease, decay, fade, disappear, vanish, to be ruined or lost; to fall from, stray from, be separated from, be deprived of, lose (with abl.); to run away, flee from (with abl.): Caus. भ्रंशयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अबभ्रंशत्, to cause to fall, throw or cast down, precipitate; to ruin, overturn, expel; to cause to be lost, cause to disappear or vanish; to cause to be separated from, deprive of (with acc. of person and abl. of thing): Desid. बिभ्रंशिषति, -ते: Intens. बाभ्रश्यते, बाभ्रष्टि, बनीभ्रश्यते, बनीभ्रंशिति, बनी-भ्रंष्टि; [cf. Angl. Sax. hreosan, resosan, ‘to fall;’ arisan, ‘to rise:’ Goth. ur-risan, us-hris-jan, af-hrisjan, ‘to cast off.’]
भ्रंश: भ्रंश, अस्, m. falling, falling off, a fall; de-clining, decline, decrease; decay, overthrow, destruc-tion, ruin (e. g. देश-भ्°, ruin of a country); dis-appearance; running away; separating from, aban-doning, deserting; losing, loss [cf. जाति-भ्°]; de-viating or straying from (propriety &c.).
भ्रंशथु: भ्रंशथु, उस्, m. = प्र-भ्रंशथु, q. v.
भ्रंशन: भ्रंशन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. the simple rt. and Caus.), causing to fall, precipitating, throwing down; (अम्), n. the act of causing to fall, precipitating; falling from, being deprived of, losing (with abl.).
भ्रंशित: भ्रंशित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Caus.), made to fall, thrown down.
भ्रंशिन्: भ्रंशिन्, ई, इनी, इ, falling, tumbling, falling down, falling out, falling from or off, coming to ruin, decaying; causing to fall, ruining, annihilating; [cf. स्वार्थ-भ्°।]
भ्रष्ट: भ्रष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, fallen, dropped, fallen down, fallen out or off; declined, decayed, ruined, disappeared, lost; fallen from, strayed from (with abl., e. g. सार्थाद् भ्रष्ट उष्ट्रः, a camel strayed from a caravan); separated from, deprived of (with abl.); depraved, vicious, a backslider; (आ), f. a fallen or unchaste woman. —भ्रष्ट-क्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has discontinued or omitted prescribed acts. —भ्रष्ट-गुद, अस्, आ, अम्, suffering from pro-lapsus ani. —भ्रष्ट-निद्र, अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of sleep. —भ्रष्ट-योग, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has fallen from devotion, a backslider. —भ्रष्ट-राज्य, अस्, आ, अम्, fallen from or deprived of a king-dom. —भ्रष्टाधिकार (°ट-अध्°), अस्, आ, अम्, fallen from office, deprived of office. —भ्रष्टा-धिकार-त्व, अम्, n. loss of office.
भ्रष्ट भ्रष्ट, भ्रष्टक। See p. 724, col. 2.
भ्रष्टक: भ्रष्टक, अस्, m., N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl., N. of his descendants.
भ्राश्य: भ्राश्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. Caus. of rt. भ्रश् or fr. rt. भ्राश् ?), Ved. to be made to fall, to be struck down; (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda X. 116, 5, भ्रा-श्यानि = आयुधानि, ‘weapons,’ and connected with rt. भ्राश्, to shine.)
भ्रंस्: भ्रंस् भ्रंस्। See rt. भ्रंश्, col. 1.
भ्रकुंश: भ्रकुंश भ्रकुंश or भ्रकुंस, अस्, m. an actor in female apparel; [cf. भृकुंश, भ्रुकुंश, भ्रूकुंश।]
भ्रकुटि: भ्रकुटि भ्र-कुटि or भ्र-कुटी = भ्रू-कुटि, इस्, f. a contraction of the eyebrows, frown. —भ्र-कुटि-मुख, अम्, n. a face with contracted eyebrows, frowning face, (also written भृकुटी-मुख।)
भ्रक्ष्: भ्रक्ष् भ्रक्ष्। See rt. भृक्ष्, p. 720.
भ्रज्: भ्रज् 1. भ्रज् in गिरि-भ्रज्, q. v.; (the word भ्रज् is thought to be fr. a lost rt. भ्रज् = Lat. frango.)
भ्रज् 2. भ्रज्, f., Ved. (perhaps) stiffness; [cf. मृत-भ्°।]
भ्रज्ज्: भ्रज्ज् 1. भ्रज्ज् (in the Dhātu-pāṭha writ-ten भ्रस्ज्; cf. rt. भृज्), cl. 6. P. A. भृज्जति, -ते (for भर्जते, see rt. भृज्), बभ्रज्ज, बभर्ज्ज, बभ्रज्जे, बभर्ज्जे, भ्रष्टा, भर्-ष्टा, भ्रक्ष्यति, -ते, भर्क्ष्यति, -ते, अभ्रा-क्षीत्, अभार्क्षीत्, अभ्रष्ट, अभर्ष्ट, भ्रष्-टुम्, भर्ष्टुम्, to fry, broil, grill, parch, scorch, roast (especially grain): Pass. भृज्ज्यते: Caus. भ्रज्जयति, भर्ज्जयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अब-भ्रज्जत्, to fry, roast: Desid. बिभ्रक्षति, -ते, बिभर्क्षति, -ते, बिभ्रज्जिषति, -ते [cf. बि-भ्रक्षु, बिभ्रज्जिषु]; Intens. बरीभृज्ज्यते, बाभ्रष्टि or बाभर्ष्टि (?); [cf. Gr. φρῡ́γ-ω, φρύγ-ανο-ν, φρύγ-ε-τρο-ν, φρυκ-τό-ς; Lat. frīg-0, frictus, frixus; Old Germ. briuwan = Angl. Sax. briwan = Old Iceland. brugga = Eng. brew; Hib. bruighim, ‘I boil, seeth.’]
2. भ्रज्ज्, भ्रट्, ट्, ट् (or भृट्, ट्, ट्, if fr. भृज्ज्, q. v.), frying, roasting, (at the end of a comp., e. g. धाना-भ्°, roasting or parching grain, see Pāṇ. VIII. 2, 36.)
भ्रज्जन: भ्रज्जन, अम्, n. the act of frying, parching, roasting; [cf. भृज्जन, भर्जन।]
भ्रष्टव्य: भ्रष्टव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be fried, to be parched or roasted.
भ्रष्टव्य भ्रष्टव्य, भ्रष्ट्र। See p. 724, col. 3.
भ्रष्ट्र: भ्रष्ट्र, अम्, n. a frying-pan, gridiron.
भ्राष्ट्र: भ्राष्ट्र, अस्, अम्, m. n. a frying-pan; (अस्), m. light, ether (in this sense probably to be con-nected with rt. भ्राश्); (अस्, ई, अम्), fried or cooked in a frying-pan. —भ्राष्ट्र-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, pro-duced or cooked in a frying-pan; (आ), f. a pan-cake made of rice-flour. —भ्राष्ट्रम्-इन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, heating the frying-pan, one who fries or cooks. —भ्राष्ट्र-व्रतिन्, ई, m. N. of a man.
भ्राष्ट्रक: भ्राष्ट्रक, अस्, अम्, m. n. a frying-pan.
भ्राष्ट्रकि: भ्राष्ट्रकि, इस्, m., N. of a man, (also read भ्राष्ट्र-कृत्।)
भ्रण्: भ्रण् भ्रण् [cf. rts. भ्रम्, रण्], cl. 1. P. भ्रणति, बभ्राण, भ्रणितुम्, to sound, utter a sound.
भ्रभङ्ग: भ्रभङ्ग भ्र-भङ्ग, अस्, m. = भ्रू-भङ्ग under भ्रू, p. 726, col. 2.
भ्रम्: भ्रम् भ्रम्, cl. 1. 4. P. (ep. also A.) भ्रमति (-ते), भ्राम्यति (-ते; accord-ing to Pāṇ. III. 1, 70, a form भ्रामति is admis-sible; the form भ्रम्यति is doubtful), बभ्राम (2nd sing. बभ्रमिथ or भ्रेमिथ, 3rd pl. बभ्रमुस् or भ्रेमुस्), भ्रमिष्यति, अभ्र-मीत्, भ्रमितुम् or भ्रान्तुम्, (perhaps orginally) to fly about humming (as insects); to roam or wander about, rove or ramble about, go or move about, (भिक्षाम् भ्रम्, to go about begging); to stroll, perambulate; to circulate, revolve, turn or whirl round, move in a circle or orbit, move round (as the stars &c.); to totter, stagger about, waver; to go astray, stray, deviate (from rectitude), err, be in error or mistake, be perplexed, be foolish or ignorant; to move to and fro, move unsteadily, flicker, flutter, vibrate, quiver (as the tongue, eyes, flames, &c.); to surround; to roam or wander through, go over (with acc., e. g. देशम् भ्रम्, to wander through a country): Caus. भ्रमयति, भ्रामयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अबिभ्रमत्, to cause or make to wander, make to rove or roam; to cause to turn round or revolve; to whirl round, swing; to cause to roll or roll along or through; to cause to err, delude, perplex, embarrass, con-fuse, seduce; to cause to move to and fro, wave, brandish, agitate, vibrate: Pass. of Caus. भ्राम्-यते, to be made to wander or whirl, caused to err, made to go astray: Desid. बिभ्रमिषति: Intens. बम्भ्रम्यते, बम्भ्रमीति, बम्भ्रान्ति, to roam about repeatedly, move frequently to and fro, wander through; [cf. Gr. βρέμ-ω, ὑψι-βρεμ-έ-της, βρόμ-ο-ς, βρον-τή, βαβράζω, πεμφρηδών, φριμάσσομαι, φόρμιγξ, ῥέμβω;Lat. frem-o, frem-or, frem-itu-s; Old Germ. brem-an, bremo, briosa; Angl. Sax. bremman; Old Iceland. brim, ‘surf.’]
भ्रम: भ्रम, अस्, m. roving or roaming about, wan-dering about; moving or going round, turning round, whirling, revolving, moving or going to and fro; straying, erring; a flickering flame (Ved.); a circular motion, whirl; a whirlpool, eddy; a potter's wheel; a lathe; a grindstone; giddiness, dizziness; wandering of mind; confusion, perplexity, error, mistake, aberration, misconception, misappre-hension, delusion [cf. स्थाणु-भ्°]; a spring, foun-tain, watercourse; (आत्), ind. by an error or mistake. —भ्रम-त्व, अम्, n. whirling found, the being in error or mistake, erroneousness. —भ्रमासक्त (°म-आस्°), अस्, m. ‘occupied in grinding,’ a knife-grinder, sword-cleaner, armourer.
भ्रमण: भ्रमण, अम्, n. (fr. the simple rt. or Caus.), the act of roaming, wandering about, travelling, tour-ing, a tour; turning round, whirling; revolution, the orbit (of a planet &c.); wavering, staggering, tottering, shaking about, unsteadiness, deviation (from rectitude); causing to go round or move about; erring, falling into error; giddiness, dizzi-ness; (ई), f. a sort of game (played by lovers, pro-bably consisting in circular movements or waltzes); a leech; N. of one of five Dhāraṇās or mental con-ceptions of the elements (viz. that of the wind; the others being स्तम्भिनी, earth; धारिणी, water; द-हनी, fire; and शोषिणी, ether). —भ्रमण-विल-सित, N. of a metre. —भ्रमणार्थे (°ण-अर्°), ind. for the sake of travelling.
भ्रमणीय: भ्रमणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be roamed about, to be wandered through.
भ्रमत्: भ्रमत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, roaming, roving, prowl-ing, wandering, sauntering about, turning round, whirling, shaking, &c. —भ्रमत्-कुटी, f. a sort of umbrella, a concave mat carried on the head; [cf. जङ्गम-कुटी।]
भ्रममाण: भ्रममाण, अस्, आ, अम्, wandering about, whirling round; being in error.
भ्रमर: भ्रमर, अस्, m. a large black bee, a kind of humble bee, any bee; a lover, gallant, libertine; a young man; a potter's wheel; a particular position of the hand; N. of a man; (आ), f. = भ्रमर-च्छल्ली below; (ई), f. a bee; the plant Jatukā, q. v.; the plant Putra-dātrī, q. v.; (अम्), n. giddi-ness, vertigo, epilepsy. —भ्रमर-करण्डक, अस्, m. a small box containing bees (used by thieves to extinguish a candle-light by letting the bees escape), a dark lantern (?). —भ्रमर-कीट, अस्, m. a species of wasp that builds its nest in the corners of walls, doors, &c., Vespa Solitaria. —भ्र-मर-कुण्ड, N. of a sacred bathing-place on the mountain Nīla (mentioned in Raghu-nātha's Rasika-ramaṇa). —भ्रमर-च्छल्ली, f. a species of creeper (= भृङ्ग-मूलिका, भृङ्गाह्वा, भ्रमरा)। —भ्रमर-पद, अम्, n. ‘bee-foot,’ a kind of metre, four times ¯˘˘¯˘¯˘˘˘˘˘˘˘˘˘¯¯¯. —भ्रमर-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘dear to bees,’ a par-ticular sort of Kadamba plant (= धारा-कदम्ब)। —भ्रमर-बाधा, f. annoyance caused by a bee, molestation by a bee. —भ्रमर-मण्डल, अम्, n. a circle or swarm of bees. —भ्रमर-मारी, f. ‘bee-killing,’ a particular plant or flower (growing in Malwa, = भृङ्ग-मारी, भ्रमरारि). —भ्र-मर-विलसित, अस्, आ, अम्, (a creeper, lotus, &c.) about which bees hover or sport; (अम्), n. the hovering or sporting of bees; (आ, अम्), f. n. a species of metre, four times ¯¯¯¯, ˘˘˘˘˘˘¯. —भ्र-मरातिथि (°र-अत्°), इस्, m. ‘bee-guest,’ the plant Michelia Champaka. —भ्रमरानन्द (°र-आन्°), अस्, m. ‘bee-joy,’ N. of several plants, Mimusops Elengi, Gærtnera Racemosa (= अतिमुक्तक), the red-flowering globe amaranth (= रक्ताम्लान)। —भ्रमराम्बा-क्षेत्र (°र-अम्°), अम्, n., N. of a district sacred to Durgā; [cf. भ्रामरी, अम्बा।] —भ्रमरारि (°र-अरि), इस्, m. ‘bee-enemy’ (= भ्रमर-मारी, q. v.). —भ्रमरालक (°र-अल्°), अस्, m. ‘bee-curl,’ a curl on the forehead. —भ्रमरावली (°र-आव्°), f. ‘bee-line,’ N. of a species of the Ati-śakkarī metre. —भ्रमराष्-टक (°र-अष्°), अम्, n. ‘eight verses on the bee,’ N. of a collection of eight verses. —भ्रमरेष्ट (°र-इष्°), अस्, m. ‘loved by bees,’ a sort of Big-nonia; (आ), f. the plant Clerodendrum Siphonanthus (= भूमि-जम्बू, q. v.). —भ्रमरोत्सवा (°र-उत्°), f. ‘bee-delight,’ the plant Gærtnera Racemosa (= माधवी).
भ्रमरक: भ्रमरक, अस्, m. a bee; a whirlpool; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a lock of hair or curl hanging down on the forehead; a humming-top; a ball for playing with; (इका), f. the act of wandering or straying in all directions. —भ्रमरिका-दृष्टि, इस्, f. a wan-dering glance (?).
भ्रमाय: भ्रमाय (fr. भ्रमत्, see Gaṇa Bhṛśādi to Pāṇ. III. 1, 12), Nom. A. भ्रमायते, &c., (pro-bably) to begin turning round or revolving; to roam about, become a vagabond.
भ्रमि: भ्रमि, इस् (according to some also भ्रमी), f. whirling or turning round, turning about, going round, circulating, revolving [cf. संवत्सर-भ्°]; a potter's wheel, a turner's lathe; a whirlpool; a whirlwind; any circular arrangement of troops, a cir-cle formed by troops; an error, a mistake; N. of a daughter of Śiśu-māra and wife of Dhruva.
भ्रमित: भ्रमित, अस्, आ, अम्, whirled round, made to go round, &c.
भ्रमिन्: भ्रमिन्, ई, इणी, इ, roaming about, going round or about, whirling round, revolving, making a circuit, turning round (as the wind), erratic.
भ्रान्त: भ्रान्त, अस्, आ, अम्, roamed, wandered (some-times impersonally, e. g. तैर् भ्रान्तम्, it has been wandered by them; and even with acc., e. g. देशम् भ्रान्तम्, it has been wandered through a country); whirled round, turned round, revolved, rolled; confused, perplexed, bewildered, gone astray, mistaken, in error, blundering; roaming or wander-ing about, turning round, whirling, rolling, stagger-ing, flying or careering round and round (as a bird), moving to and fro; (अस्), m. an elephant in rut; a species of thorn-apple, = राज-धुस्तूरक; (अम्), n. roaming, wandering about, moving to and fro; a particular mode of fighting; error, mistake, delusion, blunder. —भ्रान्त-चित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, confused or perplexed in mind. —भ्रान्त-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, confused in intellect, perplexed in mind, puzzled.
भ्रान्त भ्रान्त, भ्राम, भ्रामर, भ्राम्-यत्, &c. See p. 725, col. 2.
भ्रान्ति: भ्रान्ति, इस्, f. the act or state of wandering about, roaming, going round, flying about, turning round, revolution, whirling, rolling, a whirl or rapid rotary motion; confusion, perplexity, delirium [cf. मति-भ्°]; error, going astray, mistake, delusion, false idea or supposition, wrong notion (e. g. पद्म-भ्रान्त्या, under the false idea of [its being] a lotus; भ्राह्मण-भ्रान्ति, the error of supposing [those works to be] Brāhmaṇas); unsteadiness; doubt, un-certainty. —भ्रान्ति-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing error or confusion. —भ्रान्ति-नाशन, अस्, m. ‘destroying error,’ an epithet of Śiva. —भ्रान्ति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, wandering or roaming about, whirling; erring, mistaken, being under a delusion, labouring under an error; entertaining a false notion; a particular figure of rhetoric (describing an error). —भ्रान्ति-हर, अस्, आ, अम्, taking away delusion, removing error; (अस्), m. a counsellor, minister.
भ्रान्त्वा: भ्रान्त्वा, ind. having wandered about, having roamed through; having whirled.
भ्राम: भ्राम, अस्, m. roaming about, wandering, un-steadiness, delusion, error, mistake.
भ्रामक: भ्रामक, अस्, इका, अम् (fr. the Caus. or fr. भ्रम), causing to whirl; causing error or mis-take, bewildering, perplexing, puzzling, deceitful, deceptive, false; (अस्), m. a sort of loadstone or magnet (so called from its causing iron to turn round); sun-flower, heliotrope; a deceiver, cheat, rogue; a jackal; (आ), f., N. of a particular plant (commonly called Laghu-dhāyaṭī).
भ्रामण: भ्रामण, अम्, n. the act of causing to turn round, swinging or turning round; (ई), f. ‘the be-wilderer,’ N. of a female demon.
भ्रामयत्: भ्रामयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, causing to turn round, whirling round, bewildering.
भ्रामर: भ्रामर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भ्रमर), relating or belonging to a bee; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a kind of magnet or loadstone [cf. भ्रामक]; (अम्), n. whirling round; dancing round; vertigo, giddiness, epilepsy; honey; a village; a kind of coitus; (ई), f. an epithet of Durgā or Pārvatī (from her having assumed the form of a bee to contend with Mahi-ṣāsura ?); a Yoginī or female attendant on Durgā.
भ्रामरिन्: भ्रामरिन्, ई, इणी, इ (fr. भ्रामर), whirling round, revolving; affected with vertigo, giddy; hav-ing epilepsy, epileptic; made of honey.
भ्रामिन्: भ्रामिन्, ई, इणी, इ, confused, perplexed.
भ्राम्यत्: भ्राम्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, roaming or rambling about, strolling about, perambulating; erring.
भ्राम्यमाण: भ्राम्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being caused to wander about, being made to whirl round, being caused to err or go astray.
भ्रमात्र: भ्रमात्र भ्रमात्र, a particular high num-ber.
भ्रश्: भ्रश् भ्रश्। See rt. भ्रंश्, p. 724, col. 1.
भ्रशिमन्: भ्रशिमन् भ्रशिमन्, आ, m. (fr. भृश), po-tency, mightiness, vehemence, violence, excessive-ness, strength.
भ्रस्ज्: भ्रस्ज् भ्रस्ज्। See rt. 1. भ्रज्ज्, p. 724, col. 2.
भ्राज्: भ्राज् 1. भ्राज् (connected with rts. राज्, भ्राश्, भ्लाश्, भ्रेज्, भृज्), cl. 1. A. भ्राजते (Ved. and ep. also P. भ्राजति), बभ्राजे (बभ्राज) or भ्रेजे (3rd pl. बभ्राजिरे or भ्रे-जिरे, Pāṇ. VI. 4, 125), भ्राजिष्यते, अभ्राजिष्ट (Ved. अभ्राट्, अभ्राजि), भ्राजितुम्, to shine, glitter, gleam, glow, flash, beam, sparkle: Caus. भ्राज-यति, -यितुम्, Aor. अबभ्राजत्, अबिभ्रजत्, to make to shine, illuminate, irradiate: Desid. बिभ्रा-जिषते: Intens. बाभ्राज्यते, बाभ्राष्टि; [cf. Gr. φλέγ-ω, φλεγ-έ-θ-ω, φλέγ-μα, φλεγ-μονή, φλεγ-υρό-ς, φλύξ: Lat. fulg-e-o, fulg-ur, ful-vu-s, flag-ra-re, flam-ma for flag-ma, flā-men for flag-men, ‘the kindler, i. e. priest:’ Goth. bairh-t-s, ‘mani-fest;’ bairhtei, ‘light:’ Angl. Sax. bearht, beorht, probably blāc, blœc-an, blīc-an: Old Germ. beraht, blanch, blich-an, blich, blic, blig: Engl. bright: Russ. blescu: Lith. blizg-ù, ‘I shine:’ Scot. breagh, ‘shining, beautiful;’ breachad, boillsg, ‘splendor;’ boillsgeach, ‘splendid.’]
2. भ्राज्, भ्राट्, f. (Pāṇ. VIII. 2, 36), Ved. light, lustre, splendor, glitter; [cf. देव-भ्°, न-भ्°।]
भ्राज: भ्राज, अस्, आ, अम्, shining, gleaming, glittering (Ved.); (अस्), m., N. of one of the seven suns; of a particular kind of fire (mentioned in Hari-vaṃśa, 1. 10467); of a Gandharva protecting the Soma (Ved.); of a work composed in Ślokas and ascribed to Kātyāyana; (अम्), n., N. of a Sāman.
भ्राजक: भ्राजक, अस्, इका, अम् (fr. the Caus.), causing to shine, illuminating, making bright (said of the digestive fire and bile as brightening the skin); (अम्), n. the bile, bilious humor, gall.
भ्राजत्: भ्राजत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, shining, gleaming, glitter-ing. —भ्राजज्-जन्मन्, आनस्, m. pl., Ved. ‘having a brilliant native place or origin, brilliant form birth,’ an epithet of the Maruts; (Sāy.) having brilliant forms (= दीप्त-शरीर). —भ्राजद्-ऋष्टि, अयस्, m. pl., Ved. ‘bright-weaponed’ (having bright gleams of lightning), an epithet of the Maruts; (Sāy. = दीप्यमानायुध।)
भ्राजथु: भ्राजथु, उस्, m. brilliance, splendor, glitter, beauty. —भ्राजथु-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, shining, beautiful (said of a woman).
भ्राजन: भ्राजन, अम्, n. (fr. the Caus.), the act of causing to shine, illuminating.
भ्राजमान: भ्राजमान, अस्, आ, अम्, shining, brilliant.
भ्राजयत्: भ्राजयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, causing to shine, illu-minating.
भ्राजस्: भ्राजस्, अस्, n., Ved. sparkling, glittering; [cf. अग्नि-भ्°।] —भ्राजस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. spark-ling, glittering; containing the word भ्राजस्. —भ्रा-जस्-विन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. = भ्राजस्-वत् above.
भ्राजिन्: भ्राजिन्, ई, इनी, इ, shining, gleaming, glittering.
भ्राजिर: भ्राजिर, आस्, m. pl., N. of a class of gods under the Manu Bhautya.
भ्राजिष्ठ: भ्राजिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (superl. fr. rt. 1. भ्राज्), shining very brightly, highly glittering or radiant; (अस्), m., N. of a son of Ghṛta-pṛṣṭha.
भ्राजिष्णु: भ्राजिष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ, shining, gleaming, splen-did, radiant, elegant; (उस्), m. an epithet of Viṣṇu; of Śiva. —भ्राजिष्णु-ता, f. radiance, brightness, splendor, splendid appearance.
भ्राजिस्: भ्राजिस्, इस्, f. = भ्राजस्, p. 725. —भ्राजिष्-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, splendid, shining.
भ्राजोभ्रादन्त्य: भ्राजोभ्रादन्त्य (?), आस्, m. pl., N. of a race.
भ्रातृ: भ्रातृ भ्रातृ, ता, m. (perhaps fr. rt. भृ, and originally meaning ‘a supporter’), a brother, uterine brother, own brother, (कु-भ्रातृ, a bad brother); an intimate friend or relation, a cousin or near relative in general, an intimate friend, (some-times used as a term of friendly address); (तरौ), m. du. brother and sister; [cf. Zend brātar: Gr. φράτηρ, φράτωρ, φρᾱτρ-ία, φρᾱ́τρ-α or φρή-τρη, φρατρίζ-ω, φρατριάζ-ω, φράτριοι θεοί: Lat. frāter, fraternu-s, frātr-ia, ‘a brother's wife:’ Umbr. frā-ter: Goth. brōthar, pl. bro-thra-hans, ‘brethren:’ Angl. Sax. bródhor: Old Germ. bruodar: Slav. brātrŭ: Lith. broter-eli-s, a diminutive; bró-li-s, ‘brother;’ brotù-szi-s, ‘a cousin:’ Old Pruss. bra-ti-s: Russ. brat: Hib. brathair.] —भ्रातुर्-जाया, f. (भ्रातुर्, gen. sing.), a brother's wife, sister-in-law. —भ्रातुष्-पुत्र, अस्, m. (भ्रातुष् for भ्रातुस्, gen. sing.), a brother's son, nephew; (ई), f. a brother's daughter, niece. —भ्रातृ-गन्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, or भ्रातृ-गन्धिक, अस्, आ, अम्, a brother only in appearance, having merely the name of brother. —भ्रातृ-ज, अस्, m. a brother's son; (आ), f. a brother's daughter. —भ्रातृ-जाया, f. a brother's wife, sister-in-law. —भ्रातृ-त्व, अम्, n. fraternity, brotherhood. —भ्रातृ-दत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, given by a brother; (अम्), n. anything given by a brother to a sister on her marriage. —भ्रातृ-द्वितीया, f. a festival on the second day in the light half of the month Kārttika (on which sisters give entertain-ments to brothers in commemoration of Yamunā's entertaining her brother Yama). —भ्रातृ-पत्नी, f. a brother's wife. —भ्रातृ-पद्म-वन, अम्, n. a group of lotus-like brethren. —भ्रातृ-पुत्र, अस्, m. a brother's son, nephew. —भ्रातृ-भगिन्यौ, du. a brother and sister. —भ्रातृ-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a brother or brothers. —भ्रातृ-वधू, ऊस्, f. a brother's wife. —भ्रातृ-वल, अस्, आ, अम्, possessing a brother or brothers. —भ्रातृ-श्व-शुर, अस्, m. a husband's eldest brother. —भ्रातृ-सिंह, अस्, m., N. of a man. —भ्रातृ-हत्या, f. fratricide.
भ्रातृक: भ्रातृक, अस्, आ, अम्, having a brother, (at the end of a comp., cf. अ-भ्°); coming from a brother, of or belonging to a brother, fraternal, brotherly (in this sense the fem. is ई).
भ्रातृव्य: भ्रातृव्य, अस्, m. a brother's son, nephew, cousin; a rival, enemy, adversary; [cf. Lat. fra-trūelis.] —भ्रातृव्य-क्षयण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. destroying rivals. —भ्रातृव्य-चातन, अस्, आ, अम्, scaring or frightening away rivals. —भ्रातृव्य-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having rivals. —भ्रातृव्य-हन्, हा, घ्नी, m. f. killing or striking down rivals (Atharva-veda X. 9, 1).
भ्रात्र: भ्रात्र, अम्, n., Ved. brotherhood, fraternity.
भ्रात्रीय: भ्रात्रीय or भ्रात्रेय, अस्, m. a (father's) brother's son, nephew; (अस्, आ, अम्), fraternal, be-longing or relating to a brother.
भ्राश्: भ्राश् भ्राश् (connected with rts. 1. भ्राज्, भ्लाश्), cl. 1. 4. A. भ्राशते, भ्राश्यते (Ved. also P. भ्राश्यति), बभ्राशे or भ्रेशे (3rd pl. बभ्राशिरे or भ्रेशिरे, Pāṇ. VI. 4, 125), भ्राशिष्यते, अभ्राशिष्ट, भ्राशितुम्, to shine, glitter, gleam, blaze: Caus. भ्राशयति, यितुम्, Aor. अबभ्राशत्, अबिभ्रशत् (Vopa-deva XVII. 3): Desid. बिभ्राशिषते: Intens. बाभ्राश्-यते, बाभ्राष्टि।
भ्राष्ट्: भ्राष्ट् भ्राष्ट्र, भ्राष्ट्रक। See p. 724, col. 3.
भ्राष्ट्रेय: भ्राष्ट्रेय भ्राष्ट्रेय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a family or race; (also भ्रास्त्रेय।)
भ्रास्: भ्रास् भ्रास्, a various reading for rt. भ्राश्, col. 1.
भ्री: भ्री भ्री, cl. 9. P. भ्रीणाति or भ्रिणाति, बिभ्राय, भ्रेष्यति, अभ्रसिहित्, भ्रे-तुम् (?), Ved. to be angry [cf. भृणीय]; to fear [cf. rt. 1. भी]; to bear, support, nourish [cf. rt. भृ]; to injure, hurt, (Sāy. = rt. हिंस्, ऋग्-वेद II. 28, 7.)
भ्रुकुंश: भ्रुकुंश भ्रुकुंश or भ्रुकुंस, अस्, m. = भ्रूकुंश, q. v.
भ्रुकुटि: भ्रुकुटि भ्रु-कुटि, इस्, or भ्रु-कुटी, f. = भ्रू-कुटि under भ्रू. —भ्रुकुटि-बन्ध, अस्, m. knitting the brows, frowning, a frown. —भ्रुकुटी-मुख, अम्, n. a face with contracted eyebrows, a frowning face; (अस्, ई, अम्), having a frowning face; (अस्), m. a kind of snake.
भ्रुड्: भ्रुड् भ्रुड्, cl. 6. P. भ्रुडति, &c., to cover; to collect.
भ्रुभङ्ग: भ्रुभङ्ग भ्रु-भङ्ग, अस्, m. = भ्रू-भङ्ग under भ्रू।
भ्रुव: भ्रुव, अस्, आ, अम्, = भ्रू at the end of an adj. comp.
भ्रू: भ्रू भ्रू, ऊस्, f. (said to be fr. rt. भ्रम्), an eyebrow, the brow; [cf. अग्रे-भ्°, सु-भ्°, भ्रौ-वेय; cf. also Zend brvat; Gr. ὀ-φρύ-ς; perhaps Lat. front(t)s = ὀφρυόεις; Old Germ. brāwa; Mod. Germ. braue; Angl. Sax. brœw; Engl. brow; Slav. brŭvĭ.] —भ्रू-कुटि, इस्, or भ्रू-कुटी, f. con-traction or knitting of the eyebrow, a frown, a look of displeasure; [cf. भृ-क्°, भ्र-क्°, भ्रु-क्°।] —भ्रूकुटी-कुटिलानन (°ल-आन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having a face wrinkled with frowns. —भ्रू-क्षे-प, अस्, m. contraction of the eyebrows, a frown. —भ्रूक्षेपालाप (°प-आल्°), अस्, m. the language of frowns. —भ्रू-चापाकृष्ट-मुक्त (°प-आक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, drawn and discharged from the bow of the eyebrows (as a glance). —भ्रू-जाह, अम्, n. the root of the eyebrows (perhaps the inner side). —भ्रू-भङ्ग or भ्रू-भेद, अस्, m. contraction of the eyebrows, a frown. —भ्रूभेदिन्, ई, इनी, इ, frowning, contracting or wrinkling the brow, attended with frowns. —भ्रू-मण्डल, अम्, n. the arch of the eyebrow. —भ्रू-मध्य, अम्, n. the interval between the eyebrows. —भ्रू-लता, f. ‘brow-creeper,’ a creeper-like eyebrow, an arched eyebrow (curving like a creeper). —भ्रू-विकार, अस्, m. ‘change of the eyebrows,’ contracting the brow, frowning. —भ्रू-विक्षेप, अस्, m. contraction of the eyebrows, a frown. —भ्रू-विचेष्टित, अम्, n. playful movement of the eyebrows. —भ्रू-विलास, अस्, m. a playful or graceful motion of the eyebrows, play or contraction of the eyebrows, amorous play of the brows.
भ्रूकुंश: भ्रूकुंश भ्रूकुंश or भ्रूकुंस, अस्, m. a male actor in female attire.
भ्रूण्: भ्रूण् भ्रूण्, cl. 10. A. भ्रूणयते, &c., to hope; to trust; to confide; to wish, desire; to fear.
भ्रूण: भ्रूण भ्रूण, अस्, m. (fr. rt. भृ; perhaps for original भूर्ण), an embryo, fetus, unborn child; a child, boy; a pregnant woman (= गर्-भिणी); a Brāhman conversant with the Vedas (?); [cf. Gr. ἔμβρυον.] —भ्रूण-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, the killer of an embryo, one who occasions or procures abortion. —भ्रूण-हति, इस्, f. the killing of an embryo. —भ्रूण-हत्या, f. the killing of an em-bryo, procuring abortion; any sin equally heinous. —भ्रूण-हन्, आ, घ्नी, m. f. the killer of an embryo, one who procures abortion.
भ्रौणघ्न: भ्रौणघ्न, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भ्रूण-हन्), re-lating to the killer of an embryo.
भ्रौणहत्य: भ्रौणहत्य, अम्, n. (fr. भ्रूण-हन्), = भ्रूण-हत्या, the killing of an embryo.
भ्रेज्: भ्रेज् भ्रेज् (allied to rt. 1. भ्राज्), cl. 1. A. भ्रेजते, बिभ्रेजे, to shine, glitter, gleam, &c.: Caus. भ्रेजयति, -यितुम्, अबिभ्रेजत्।
भ्रेष्: भ्रेष् भ्रेष् [cf. rts. भ्रंश्, ह्रेष्], cl. 1. P. A. भ्रेषति, -ते, बिभ्रेष, बि-भ्रेषे, भ्रेषितुम्, to go, move; to totter, waver, slip, fall, make a false step; to fear; to be angry.
भ्रेष: भ्रेष, अस्, m. motion, going, proceeding; tot-tering, wavering, slipping, falling, declining or falling (from virtue), deviation (from rectitude), trespass, sin; loss, deprivation.
भ्रेषण: भ्रेषण, अम्, n. the act of going, moving, tottering, &c.
भौवेय: भौवेय भ्रौवेय, अस्, m. (fr. भ्रू), a me-tronymic.
भ्लक्ष्: भ्लक्ष् भ्लक्ष् (various reading for rt. भक्ष्; cf. rt. भ्रक्ष्), cl. 1. P. A. भ्लक्षति, -ते, &c., to eat.
भ्लाश्: भ्लाश् भ्लाश् (connected with rt. भ्राश्), cl. 1. 4. A. भ्लाशते, भलाश्यते, ब-भ्लाशे or भलेशे (3rd pl. बभ्लाशिरे or भ्लेशिरे), भ्लाशितुम्, to shine, gleam, beam, glitter, &c.
भ्लास्: भ्लास् भ्लास्, a various reading for rt. भ्लाश् above.
भ्लेष्: भ्लेष् भ्लेष्, cl. 1. P. A. भ्लेषति, -ते, &c., = rt. भ्रेष्, to go; to fear, &c.
